subject: Re: Enterprisecorp - stakeholder map, procurement steps & exception request
messages:
From: John Smith <john.smith@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@enterprisecorp.com>, procurement@enterprisecorp.com
Date: Fri, 28 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up & buying process details from today's call

Marissa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo today - the model latency and cost numbers looked good. Per our discussion, here's the high-level of how procurement and legal typically engage at Enterprisecorp:

- Technical eval by Security (Emily) and Infra (internal) takes ~2-3 weeks.
- Commercial + Procurement review (standard 60-day POs) but they can escalate for strategic vendors.
- Final approval sits with Finance (CFO) for T&C changes or multi-year commitments.

Primary asks from my side:
1) Can you send a stakeholder map and recommended procurement path (who should we loop, approvals required)?
2) We may need an SLA exception for the uptime window and a custom data retention term - if so what internal approvals are needed?

I'll loop procurement and Emily on next steps.

Thanks,
John
Director of Product, Enterprisecorp

Attachment: Enterprisecorp_RFP_excerpt.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@enterprisecorp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up & buying process details from today's call

John - great to meet you. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap:
- Enterprisecorp is evaluating for customer-facing features (real-time chat + summarization).
- Primary success metrics: sub-200ms 95th pct latency, < $0.01 per 1k tokens target at scale, and SOC2-compliant handling of PII.

Stakeholder map (proposed):
- Technical / Security: Emily Tan (primary), Neha Kapoor (Redwood security lead to engage)
- Procurement: procurement@enterprisecorp.com (commercial terms)
- Economic buyer: Robert Hayes, CFO (final approval on deviations)
- Day-to-day champion: John Smith

Procurement steps we recommend:
1) Security questionnaire (we provide SOC2 artifacts, SIEM logs sample)
2) Commercial review (standard SOW / PO)
3) If contract needs SLA / payment term exceptions, Redwood requests internal approval (we'll flag as an exception)

Ask: Can you confirm that the above stakeholder list is correct and whether your procurement requires formal approval letters for exceptions?

Next: Vivek will prepare a one-pager on proposed commercial terms. I'll loop Neha on the security artifacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Enterprisecorp_Stakeholder_Map.xlsx

From: Emily Tan <emily.tan@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@enterprisecorp.com>, procurement@enterprisecorp.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up & buying process details from today's call

Thanks - stakeholder map looks right. A couple of clarifications from Security:

- We'll need SOC2 Type II report and a short architecture diagram showing where data flows and how keys are managed.
- For PII handling we prefer customer-controlled KMS or a written attestation of ephemeral cache behavior.
- If Redwood requires any SLA deviations (e.g., credits or extended RTO), our procurement will escalate to legal and finance.

Please loop your security lead (Neha) and attach SOC2 details. Also, we typically require procurement to see any proposed exceptions in writing before formal review.

Thanks,
Emily
Principal Security Engineer, Enterprisecorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Enterprisecorp - internal: request for procurement/SLA exception approval

Team - quick internal thread to get aligned. Enterprisecorp is asking us to provide:

1) SOC2 artifacts + architecture diagram (we can provide)
2) A written request describing any SLA / payment-term exceptions they might ask procurement to approve. Potential asks we should prepare for:
   - SLA: specific credit structure for <99.9% monthly uptime (they may request stronger uptime or different credit tiers)
   - Payment terms: they asked if 60-day PO terms are acceptable; our standard is Net30.
   - Data retention/KMS: they may request customer-managed KMS or a carveout in retention.

Proposal: we proactively provide SOC2 and arch diagram, and pre-authorize the following exceptions for commercial speed:
- Discount cap: up to 18% off list for multi-year committed seats (requires LA approval)
- Payment terms: allow Net45 for deals under $250K; Net60 needs VP-level signoff
- SLA exceptions: we can offer a custom SLA with standard credit tiers; deeper uptime commitments require PM+Legal signoff.

Please reply if you approve the above guardrails or suggest adjustments. If approved, I will draft the formal exception request (SLA_Exception_Request.pdf) to share with Enterprisecorp procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enterprisecorp - internal: request for procurement/SLA exception approval

Marissa - thanks for the clear proposal. I support the suggested guardrails with one modification:

- Discount cap: reduce to 15% for initial approval; anything above 15% routes to CRO (Laurence) - that keeps us conservative during early sales cycles.
- Payment terms: Net45 OK up to $300K; Net60 needs VP Finance approval (same as you suggested).
- SLA exceptions: approve drafting a custom SLA to share with Enterprisecorp; any changes to uptime targets that imply penalty increases should be reviewed by Legal.

Aditya, please confirm if we have any known operational constraints for sub-200ms 95th pct on their expected load profile (John provided scale estimates in the RFP excerpt). Neha, please coordinate SOC2 + KMS guidance and prepare a short attestation we can send publicly.

I'll approve the internal exception request with the adjusted discount cap. Marissa, you can proceed to draft the exception doc and send to procurement.

- Laura
VP, Sales Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Enterprisecorp - Exception request & next steps

John / Emily / Procurement team - thanks for the prompt details. Per our internal review we've attached the formal exception request and SOC2 artifacts. Summary of what we're proposing: 

- Commercial: Net45 payment terms (up to $300K) and a one-time 15% discount on list for the first-year committed seats.
- SLA: Draft custom SLA attached. Standard credit tiers apply; no changes to indemnity.
- Security: SOC2 Type II and a short attestation on ephemeral cache and key management attached. We are not offering customer-managed KMS in the hosted product; we can discuss private deployment options if that's a hard requirement.

Attachments: Proposal-Redwood-Enterprise-2026.pdf, SLA_Exception_Request.pdf, SOC2_Type_II_redacted.pdf

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm receipt and timing for formal review.
2) Security: confirm if our attestation is sufficient or if you need additional artifacts.
3) John: if you need us to loop Finance (Robert Hayes) for accelerated decisioning, let us know and we can request exec alignment.

Thanks - looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
